verdict.rationale: Databricks documents Genie and Genie One, which let business users ask natural-language data questions and get answers grounded in organizational data, returned with the SQL queries and results. It also documents a metric-view semantic layer where the query engine generates the correct computation, and Unity Catalog access control on every query. However, the evidence never states that Genie answers are routed through metric views, nor that joins are constrained, so the 'semantically-grounded rather than hallucinated joins' part is only implied. missing for 10: documentation that Genie uses metric views or semantic definitions to ground its SQL, evidence of join or accuracy safeguards against hallucinated joins, independent or hands-on corroboration of answer correctness.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, business users can ask questions in natural language and get governed, semantically-grounded answers rather than hallucinated joins

citations.quote: Ask data questions in natural language and get answers grounded in your organization's data.
Navigate the Genie One interface designed for business users. View dashboards, ask natural language data questions, and discover assets shared with you.
users ask questions of their data and get back SQL queries, results tables, and visualizations
you define the metric once, for example sum of revenue divided by distinct customer count, and users can group by any available field. The query engine generates the correct computation.
Unity Catalog operates beneath every data and AI interaction in your workspaces automatically: enforcing access control when you query a table or call a model
